$comment: The contract for the regions in depth (codex39). One fragment per atlas sheet at .scripts/regions/fragments/<sheet>.json, plus mapless.json. build-regions.cjs merges them into js/data-regions.js; check-fragment.cjs proves one fragment, check-regions.js the built file. Every string is British, dash free (no U+2014, no U+2013, no entity, no spaced double hyphen), carries nothing at or above U+2190, and never the word practice or practise (use rehearse, drill, study). An empty field is a true answer: write nothing you are not sure of.

fragment.sheet: the atlas sheet id (france, italy, spain, portugal, germany, austria, california, oregon, washington, new-york, argentina, chile, australia, new-zealand, south-africa, hungary, greece); mapless.json has no sheet and holds countries only
fragment.regions: one region record per ATLAS_V2.sheets[sheet].regions entry, in map order
fragment.aliases: an object: folded alias (lower case, accents stripped, punctuation out) to a slug or a country key, for every sub-region, appellation, village or district a house wine's region string or a question might name (medoc, pauillac, cote de nuits, chablis, langhe, rioja alta, ...). A name that is itself an article's name needs no alias.
fragment.terroirRows: an object: the exact TERROIR row name (its r field) to a slug, for every TERROIR row of this country
fragment.cats: an object: a Village PRIMERS cat or a Regionale INTRO_PRIMERS id that names a place in this country, to the list of slugs it covers

region.slug: unique across the whole file, /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, the region's folded name (burgundy, cote-du-rhone is wrong, use rhone), prefixed by the country only when two countries share a name
region.name: exactly ATLAS_V2's region name for this index
region.index: the region's position in ATLAS_V2.sheets[sheet].regions, from 0
region.asked: the levels whose exam asks about this region: a non-empty subset of ["intro","certified","advanced","master"], in that order
region.summary: 60 to 120 words: what a server must hold in the head, in four to six sentences

terroir.water: 0 to 120 words: rivers, lakes, seas and their effect, or empty

grapes.name: a grape name as GRAPES, GRAPES_PLUS or INTRO_GRAPES spell it, else plain: 1
grapes.plain: 1 only when the name is in no grape list
grapes.styles: one or two sentences on what it makes here

wines.style: the wine as the list names it (Chablis, Barolo, Brut NV)
wines.colour: white | red | rose | sparkling | sweet | fortified | orange
wines.note: one to three sentences: what it tastes like, how it is served, what it goes with

made.viticulture: 60 to 250 words: training, density, harvest, the hazards, the choices that mark the region
made.winemaking: 60 to 250 words: the techniques that mark the region (method, vessel, lees, oak, blending, ageing rules, sweetening, fortification)

law.classification: 40 to 200 words: the system in prose
tiers: what it means, with the rule that matters on an exam

places.name: a sub-region, village, district or cru
places.depth: optional: advanced | master when the exam asks it only from that level
places.places: optional nested places of the same shape

producers.id: a WINE_PRODUCERS id when the Codex holds the house (p-...), else omitted
producers.name: the house's name
producers.why: one sentence: why a sommelier knows it

exam: 3 to 8 lines: what the exam asks about this region, as a study prescription
traps: 3 to 8 lines: the confusions and the false friends
say: its respelling in the house style: mar-SHAHN duh VAN, burr BLAHN, caps on the stressed syllable
region.questions: 6 to 8, at least 3 multiple choice. MC: {cat, q, opts: [4 strings], a: index, exp}. SA: {cat, q, sa: 1, accept: [2 to 8 strings the grader accepts, the canonical answer first, accents both ways], ans: 'the canonical answer', exp}. cat is the region's name. No id: the builder mints r- ids. One fact per stem; no NOT, EXCEPT or all of the above; distractors of one kind and each a real thing; exp says why in one or two sentences

country.key: the sheet id, or for a mapless country its folded name (canada, england, switzerland, eastern-europe, lebanon, uruguay, mexico)
country.name: the country's name as a reader says it
country.sheet: the sheet id, or omitted for a mapless country
country.mapless: 1 for a country with no map sheet, else omitted
country.overview: 200 to 500 words in paragraphs separated by a blank line: the country's wine story, its geography, the shape of its law, what the exam leans on
country.regionsOrder: for a sheet: every region slug of the sheet in map order; for a mapless country: empty
country.places: mapless countries only: the regions, as region-shaped place entries [{name, note, depth?, places?}]
country.questions: 6 to 8, as a region's; cat is the country's name

floors.region.prose.total: 900 to 1,600 words over summary, terroir, made, law.classification, wines notes and places notes
floors.country.prose.total: 400 to 1,200 words over summary, overview and places notes
